page.after:
What the differences mean

Where the line is: two cameras, front and rear, sold as one set at or under $150 at the maker's US store on 2026-11-21, during the Black Friday sales. Dealectric does not test units; every figure here is a maker's or a named reviewer's.

  • Parking mode is the cost outside the sticker. All four need a hardwire kit to record while parked. Only the 70mai A810 Lite set has it in the price: $129.99 with the rear camera, a 64 GB card and the UP03 kit, so $150 − $129.99 = $20.01 to spare.
  • Vantrue S1 Pro 2CH: the Vantrue kit that names it is $29.99, so the cameras would have to cost $150 − $29.99 = $120.01 or less to fit with it. On 2026-11-21 they were {after:vantrue-s1-pro-2ch}. {buy:vantrue-s1-pro-2ch}
  • 70mai A810: $129.99 + $27.99 (UP03) = $157.98, which is $7.98 over.
  • Botslab G980H: its fuse-tap kit is $44.99, so the cameras would have to cost $150 − $44.99 = $105.01 or less. The store price on 2026-11-21 was {price:botslab-g980h-4k-2k-dual-dash-cam}. {buy:botslab-g980h-4k-2k-dual-dash-cam}
  • Frame rate with both cameras on: Product Bible lists the S1 Pro at 30 fps on both channels; DashCamTalk found the A810 at 25 fps on both once the rear is attached. 30 − 25 = 5 more frames every second on the Vantrue.

Left out for being just over the line: the 70mai A810S. 70mai's store lists it from $139.99 and sells its RC24 rear camera at $19.99, $159.98 for the pair, and DashCamTalk lists the A810S at $159.99. It has a supercapacitor, the IMX678 in front and a Sony IMX662 rear camera at 1080p HDR 30 fps, so if a two-camera A810S is at or under $150 on the day you buy, take it over everything in the table. Also over: the DDPAI N5 Pro (4K front + 2K rear, 64 GB built in) at {after:ddpai-n5-pro} through our link ({buy:ddpai-n5-pro}), and the VIOFO A229 Plus 2CH, $159.99 on Amazon in Product Bible's 2026-11-19 check.

What parking mode adds to each price

A dash cam plugged into the 12 V socket switches off with the car. To record a bump or a break-in while parked, it needs a hardwire kit: a cable to the fuse box that keeps the camera powered and cuts it off before the car battery runs down. Vantrue's Voltage Display Hardwire Kit lets you set that cut-off at 11.6, 12 or 12.4 V. Each maker sells its own kit, and the price varies more than the cameras do:

  • Vantrue: Voltage Display Hardwire Kit, $29.99 (list $34.99), USB-C; its listing names the S1 Pro. The S1 Pro's listing gives up to 15 seconds of pre-event footage in parking mode.
  • 70mai: UP03, $27.99, for USB-C dash cams. 70mai's A810 page says UP03 is required for all parking functions and is sold separately. The A810 Lite listing marks parking protection "Hardwire Kit required" and sells a Front + Rear Cam + 64GB + UP03 set at $129.99.
  • Botslab: Type-C Hardwire Kit with Fuse Tap, $44.99 (list $54.99); its listing names the G980H. Botslab's spec page says "Hard Wire Kit: Not Included".

All kit prices were read on the makers' stores on 2026-11-21. None of these totals counts a memory card where one is not in the box: the Vantrue and the A810 ship without one.

Not recommended for a car parked in the sun: 70mai A810

The A810 looks like the bargain here: the same Sony STARVIS 2 IMX678 front sensor as dearer cameras for $129.99 with the rear camera. But 70mai's own spec table lists a 500 mAh battery, and DashCamTalk calls that "not ideal in hot climates". DashCamTalk also found the front camera drops from 30 to 25 fps once the rear is connected, and names the rear sensor as a SmartSens SC200AI, so the Sony claim covers the front channel only. In a mild climate it is the sharpest front camera in this table; in a hot one, pick a supercapacitor model.
